key_insight: MatToolBench shows that multimodal agents that excel on general software benchmarks still struggle badly with real materials-science workflows because the bottlenecks are domain knowledge, tool-specific conventions, and cross-tool coordination—not just visual grounding.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark gives engineers a realistic way to measure and improve AI assistants for scientific software, script-driven analysis, and database querying in materials research.
method: Built a real-environment benchmark with 204 tasks spanning 10 materials-science tools in three modes: GUI操作, OriginPro scripting, and code-based database queries.
Executed tasks inside a Windows 11 VM and used expert-defined sub-criteria for partial-credit scoring.
Validated a multimodal judge for OriginPro figure aesthetics with a human-LLM agreement study.
evidence_signal: The evaluation pipeline reports an average GUI scoring F1 of 0.98, while the strongest model achieved only 25% success on GUI tasks and 45% on code tasks.
watch_item: Results may depend on the specific Windows 11 VM setup and the limited tool set, so transfer to other scientific software stacks should be tested carefully.
paper_title: MatToolBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents in Real-World Materials Science Workflows
